title: Saʿādat, maʿāli, sumuww: titles at work
goal: At the office, Maryam briefs you before a director general's visit: which title goes in writing, what to call him, and what not to say
tip: Titles go before a post or a name, in writing and formal speech: saʿādat il-mudīr il-ʿāmm, maʿāli l-wazīr. Face to face, the spoken honorific is enough: ṭāl ʿumrak. To check what to say, ask shu ngūl-lah?: shu ngūl-lah fi l-īmēl? 'what do we call him in the email?'
grammar: honorifics: written titles (saʿādat, maʿāli, sumuww) vs the spoken ṭāl ʿumrak
dialogue: A
باكر يزورنا المدير العام من الحكومة، واستقباله مسؤوليتنا كلنا
bāchir yzūrna l-mudīr il-ʿāmm min il-ḥukūma, w istiqbālah masʼūliyyatna killna
Tomorrow the director general from the government is visiting us, and welcoming him is all of our responsibility.
B
زين، يا ترا شو نقول له؟ يا شيخ؟
zēn, yā tara shu ngūl-lah? yā shēkh?
OK, I wonder, what do we call him? Yā shēkh?
A
لا، هو مب شيخ. في الإيميل نكتب «سعادة المدير العام»، وقدامه نقول طال عمرك
la, huwa mub shēkh. fi l-īmēl niktib "saʿādat il-mudīr il-ʿāmm", w jiddāmah ngūl ṭāl ʿumrak
No, he isn't a sheikh. In the email we write "His Excellency the Director General", and to his face we say ṭāl ʿumrak.
B
وإذا زارنا وزير؟ نكتب نفس اللقب؟
w idha zārna wazīr? niktib nafs il-laqab?
And if a minister visits us? Do we write the same title?
A
لا، للوزير نكتب «معالي الوزير». و«سمو الشيخ» للشيوخ من الأسر الحاكمة
la, lil-wazīr niktib "maʿāli l-wazīr". w "sumuww ish-shēkh" lish-shyūkh min il-usar il-ḥākma
No, for a minister we write "His Excellency the Minister". And "His Highness the Sheikh" is for sheikhs from the ruling families.
B
فهمت. يعني الألقاب في الكتابة والكلام الرسمي؟
fhimt. yaʿni l-alqāb fi l-kitāba w il-kalām ir-rasmi?
I see. So the titles are for writing and formal speech?
A
هيه. على كل حال، في الكلام طال عمرك وبس. لا تقول له يا ريّال!
hē. ʿala kill ḥāl, fi l-kalām ṭāl ʿumrak w bas. la tgūl-lah yā rayyāl!
Yes. Anyway, when you're talking, just ṭāl ʿumrak. Don't call him yā rayyāl!
B
صدقيني، ولا برو بعد! بكون رسمي من أول ما يدخل
ṣaddgīni, wala brō baʿad! bakūn rasmi min awwal ma yidkhil
Believe me, no "bro" either! I'll be formal from the moment he walks in.
A
زين. وعلى ما يبدو، هو يحب يسمع الشباب يتكلمون عربي
zēn. w ʿala ma yibdu, huwa yḥibb yismaʿ ish-shabāb yitkallamūn ʿarabi
Good. And it seems he likes hearing young people speak Arabic.
items: (recognise); in writing, before the post or name of an undersecretary, an ambassador or a director general; not for an ordinary manager
(recognise); for crown princes, deputy rulers and other senior members of the ruling families; a ruler is ṣāḥib is-sumuww
one: il-laqab (اللقب); q kept, as in fuṣḥā
culture: In official UAE writing, titles come before the name. Ṣāḥib is-sumuww (His Highness) is for the President and the rulers; sumuww for other senior members of the ruling families, such as crown princes and deputy rulers. Maʿāli (His Excellency) goes with ministers and those of their rank, saʿādat with undersecretaries, ambassadors and many directors general. Use sheikh only for a real sheikh.

title: Taking your leave, the old way
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Rāshid there, hear how visitors entered and left a sheikh's majlis in the old days, and take your leave the same way
tip: Before leaving an elder or a host, ask, don't announce: ṭāl ʿumrak, idha ma shay lāzim, binitrakhkhaṣ? 'sir, if there's nothing you need, may we take our leave?'. The host may keep you (igʿid 'stay') or let you go with allāh ywaffigkum, and you answer āmīn.
grammar: taking leave from an elder: ṭāl ʿumrak, idha ma shay lāzim, binitrakhkhaṣ?
dialogue: A
أيام أول، إذا رحت مجلس الشيخ، تقول للعسكري عند الباب: أنا فلان بن فلان
ayyām awwal, idha riḥt majlis ish-shēkh, tgūl lil-ʿaskari ʿind il-bāb: ana fulān bin fulān
In the old days, if you went to the sheikh's majlis, you told the guard at the door: I'm so-and-so, son of so-and-so.
B
وهو يدخلك على طول؟
w huwa ydakhkhlak ʿala ṭūl?
And he let you straight in?
A
لا، يستأذن الشيخ أول. والشيوخ يعرفون كل واحد من أبوه ولبوقته
la, yistaʼdhin ish-shēkh awwal. w ish-shyūkh yaʿarfūn kill wāḥid min ubūh w labbūgtah
No, he asked the sheikh's permission first. And the sheikhs knew everyone by his father and his family nickname.
B
ها؟ وإذا دخلت، أقعد على طول؟
hā? w idha dakhalt, agʿid ʿala ṭūl?
Huh? And once I'm in, do I sit down straight away?
A
لا يا ولدي، المجلس له هيبة، وهذي تقاليدنا: ما تقعد لين يقول لك الشيخ تفضل
la yā wildi, il-majlis lah hēba, w hādhi tagālīdna: ma tigʿid lēn ygūl-lak ish-shēkh tfaẓẓal
No, son, the majlis commands respect, and these are our traditions: you don't sit until the sheikh says "please".
B
وشلون الواحد يطلع؟ يا ترا لازم يستأذن؟
w shlōn il-wāḥid yiṭlaʿ? yā tara lāzim yistaʼdhin?
And how does one leave? I wonder, does he have to ask permission?
A
تقول: طال عمرك، إذا ما شي لازم، بنترخص؟ والشيخ يقول: اقعد، ولّا الله يوفقكم
tgūl: ṭāl ʿumrak, idha ma shay lāzim, binitrakhkhaṣ? w ish-shēkh ygūl: igʿid, walla allāh ywaffigkum
You say: "Sir, if there's nothing you need, may we take our leave?" And the sheikh says "Stay", or "God grant you success".
B
الظاهر إن الوقت تأخر. طال عمرك، إذا ما شي لازم، بنترخص؟
iẓ-ẓāhir inn il-wagt taʼakhkhar. ṭāl ʿumrak, idha ma shay lāzim, binitrakhkhaṣ?
It looks like it's getting late. Sir, if there's nothing you need, may we take our leave?
A
وين؟ بدري! بس يلا، الله يوفقكم
wēn? badri! bas yalla, allāh ywaffigkum
What, already? It's early! But off you go; God grant you success.
B
آمين يا عمي، الله يحفظك
āmīn yā ʿammi, allāh yiḥfaẓak
Amen, uncle. God keep you.
items: may we take our leave? may we go now? (respectful)
it commands respect (a place or a person) (a masculine thing)
a feminine thing: lha hēba (لها هيبة)
a family nickname, a byname passed down in a family (old-fashioned)
(recognise); his family nickname: labbūgtah (لبوقته); UAE also: it-taʿyūra (التعيورة)
culture: In the old days, a visitor to a ruler's majlis gave his name at the gate as fulān bin fulān, and the guard asked the sheikh's permission to let him in. The sheikhs knew people by their father's or grandfather's name. Inside, you didn't sit until the sheikh invited you, or speak until he spoke to you, and to leave you asked his permission first.

title: Labbēh, ṭāl ʿumrak!
goal: At the office, your manager Bū Saʿīd calls you in before a meeting: answer the way you answer a senior, take his requests, and offer more help
tip: When an elder or a senior calls your name, answer labbēh 'yes? at your service', not shu?. Take a request with samm ṭāl ʿumrak or min ʿyūni 'gladly', and offer more: tāmirni ʿala shay thāni? 'anything else I can do for you?'. He may thank you with allāh yirẓa ʿalēk 'bless you'.
grammar: answering a senior: labbēh, samm ṭāl ʿumrak, min ʿyūni, tāmirni ʿala shay thāni?
dialogue: A
سالم! تعال لو سمحت، أبيك دقيقة
Sālim! taʿāl law samaḥt, abīk dagīga
Sālim! Come here, please; I need you for a minute.
B
لبيه طال عمرك
labbēh ṭāl ʿumrak
Yes, sir?
A
الاجتماع بعد ساعة، وعلى ما يبدو المدير العام بيحضر. التقرير ضروري
il-ijtimāʿ baʿd sāʿa, w ʿala ma yibdu l-mudīr il-ʿāmm biyiḥẓar. it-taqrīr ẓarūri
The meeting's in an hour, and it seems the director general will be there. The report is essential.
B
سم طال عمرك، الحين أطبعه وأييبه لك
samm ṭāl ʿumrak, il-ḥīn aṭbaʿah w ayībah lak
Right away, sir; I'll print it now and bring it to you.
A
وطرش نسخة لمريم، عشان تراجع التفاصيل قبل الاجتماع
w ṭarrish nuskha l-Maryam, ʿashān trājiʿ it-tafāṣīl gabil il-ijtimāʿ
And send a copy to Maryam, so she can go over the details before the meeting.
B
حاضر. تامرني على شي ثاني؟
ḥāẓir. tāmirni ʿala shay thāni?
Certainly. Anything else I can do for you?
A
وقول للشباب إن الاجتماع بيتأخر ربع ساعة، الظروف جي
w gūl lish-shabāb inn il-ijtimāʿ biyitʼakhkhar rubʿ sāʿa, iẓ-ẓurūf chī
And tell the lads the meeting will start a quarter of an hour late; that's how things are.
B
من عيوني، الحين أقول لهم
min ʿyūni, il-ḥīn agūl-lhum
Gladly; I'll tell them now.
A
ما قصرت يا ولدي، الله يرضى عليك
mā gaṣṣart yā wildi, allāh yirẓa ʿalēk
Thank you, son; bless you.
B
ما سوينا شي، وإياك. صدقني هذا واجبي
mā sawwēna shay, w iyyāk. ṣaddigni hādha wājbi
It's nothing, and bless you too. Believe me, it's my job.
items: yes? at your service (answering when an elder or a senior calls you)
right away, sir; certainly (respectful) (to a man)
to a woman: samm ṭāl ʿumrich (سم طال عمرج)
anything else I can do for you? (lit. do you order me anything else?) (to a man)
to a woman: tāmrīni ʿala shay thāni? (تامريني على شي ثاني؟)
gladly, with pleasure (lit. from my eyes)

title: Oops, sorry! Bravo!
goal: At a five-a-side pitch, your classmate Mājid reacts to the game with English interjections; agree which ones you'd keep away from your lecturers
tip: With friends your age, borrowed interjections are normal: ūps!, sōri, wāw!, brāvo ʿalēk!, yēs!. With older people, switch to the Arabic ones: is-samūḥa for sōri, yā salām for wāw. Your rule: il-ingilīzi lil-malʿab, w il-ʿarabi lil-muḥāẓra.
grammar: borrowed interjections (sōri, ūps, wāw, brāvo) and their Arabic counterparts
dialogue: A
أوبس! سوري، الكورة ضربتك؟
ūps! sōri, il-kūra ẓarbatak?
Oops! Sorry, did the ball hit you?
B
عادي، ما صار شي. جولة ثانية؟
ʿādi, ma ṣār shay. jōla thānya?
It's fine, nothing happened. Another round?
A
يلا دورك. واو! شو هالضربة! تحفة!
yalla dōrak. wāw! shu haẓ-ẓarba! tuḥfa!
Go on, your turn. Wow! What a shot! Brilliant!
B
يس! أول هدف لي اليوم
yēs! awwal hadaf li l-yōm
Yes! My first goal today!
A
برافو عليك يا البطل! غلبتني، صرت محترف
brāvo ʿalēk yā l-baṭal! ghalabtni, ṣirt miḥtarif
Bravo, champ! You beat me; you've turned pro.
B
ها؟ لا تبالغ، بس حظ
hā? la tbālig, bas ḥaẓẓ
Eh? Don't exaggerate; it was just luck.
A
أوه نو! الكورة طلعت برا الملعب
ōh nō! il-kūra ṭilʿat barra l-malʿab
Oh no! The ball's gone out of the pitch.
B
أنا بييبها. بس قدام الدكتور ما بقول سوري، بقول السموحة
ana bayībha. bas jiddām id-daktōr ma bagūl sōri, bagūl is-samūḥa
I'll get it. But in front of the lecturer I won't say "sorry", I'll say is-samūḥa.
A
صح، ويقول لك ما عليه. وبدال واو قول يا سلام
ṣaḥḥ, w ygūl-lak ma ʿalēh. w badāl wāw gūl yā salām
Right, and he'll say ma ʿalēh, "no problem". And instead of "wow" say yā salām.
B
فهمت: الإنقليزي للملعب، والعربي للمحاضرة!
fhimt: il-ingilīzi lil-malʿab, w il-ʿarabi lil-muḥāẓra!
Got it: English for the pitch, Arabic for the lecture hall!
items: with older people: is-samūḥa or āsif
bravo! well done! (friends only) (to a man)
culture: Young Emiratis switch between Emirati Arabic, fuṣḥā and English every day, and their speech mixes them: Arabic interjections in English sentences, and trendy English expressions in Emirati Arabic. Older people, Emiratis and other Arabs alike, tend to see this mixing as bad Arabic, which is one reason to keep the English for friends.
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner (search a tutoring site for «Emirati Arabic tutor»), talk for 10 minutes about a match you watched or played. React the way friends do (sōri, wāw!, yēs!). Then retell the best moment for 2 minutes as if to Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Arabic reactions only (is-samūḥa, yā salām, mā shāʼ allāh).

title: Khaṭīr! Rāshid's new words
goal: Rāshid shows you a video of a new burger place, full of the words young people use now; work out what they mean and where you can say them
tip: Young people's praise words often mean the opposite of the dictionary: khaṭīr 'dangerous' means 'amazing', mub ṭabīʿi 'not normal' means 'unreal'. Keep them for friends, not the office. You'll hear la tṣīr ōfar 'don't go over the top'; to calm a friend down yourself, la tbālig is enough.
grammar: trendy language: falla, stāyl, ōfar (recycle khaṭīr, mub ṭabīʿi) (friends only)
dialogue: A
شوف هالفيديو! المطعم اليديد في الجميرا، البرقر خطير
shūf hal-fīdyo! il-maṭʿam il-yidīd fi l-Jimēra, il-burgar khaṭīr
Look at this video! The new restaurant in Jumeirah: the burger's insane.
B
ها؟ يعني فيه شي غلط؟
hā? yaʿni fīh shay ghalaṭ?
Huh? You mean something's wrong with it?
A
لا! يعني وايد حلو. والمكان مب طبيعي
la! yaʿni wāyid ḥilu. w il-makān mub ṭabīʿi
No! It means really good. And the place is unreal.
B
سوري، هذي كلمات يديدة علي!
sōri, hādhi kalimāt yidīda ʿalay!
Sorry, these words are new to me!
A
هذي كلماتنا الحين. والجو هناك فلة، والديكور ستايل. واو!
hādhi kalimātna l-ḥīn. w il-jaww hnāk falla, w id-dīkōr stāyl. wāw!
That's how we talk now. And the vibe there is great fun, and the décor's stylish. Wow!
B
وأقدر أقول هالكلام في الدوام؟
w agdar agūl hal-kalām fi d-dawām?
And can I say this stuff at work?
A
لا لا، مديرك بيقول: لا تصير أوفر! خلها ويا الشباب
la la, mudīrak biygūl: la tṣīr ōfar! khallha wiyya sh-shabāb
No, no, your boss would say "don't go over the top!" Save it for the lads.
B
ومع هذا، لا تبالغ، باقي ما ذقناه
w maʿa hādha, la tbālig, bāgi ma dhugnāh
Still, don't exaggerate; we haven't tried it yet.
A
خلاص، الخميس نروح كلنا، وانت قول لي إذا خطير ولّا لا
khalāṣ, il-khamīs nrūḥ killna, w inta gūl-li idha khaṭīr walla la
Fine, let's all go on Thursday, and you tell me if it's insane or not.
B
اتفقنا! وأنا بحكم على الديكور
ittafagna! w ana baḥkum ʿala d-dīkōr
Deal! And I'll be the judge of the décor.
items: great fun, a great vibe (friends only)
don't go over the top, don't overdo it (friends only) (to a man)
to a woman: la tṣīrīn ōfar (لا تصيرين أوفر); (recognise)

title: Sufra dāyma!
goal: At lunch in Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Rāshid there, praise the fish he caught and his cooking, thank him the way guests do, and refuse a third helping politely
tip: Praise the host with ma ʿalēk zōd 'nobody does it better', and refuse more with allāh la yhīnak, bas shbaʿt. When you've finished, thank him for the meal with sufra dāyma 'may your table always be full'; he answers dāyma b-wjūdkum.
grammar: thanks and praise for a host: ma ʿalēk zōd, allāh la yhīnak, sufra dāyma (recycle: tislam īdak)
dialogue: A
تفضلوا، الغدا جاهز. هالهامور صدته بإيدي الصبح
tfaẓẓalu, il-ghada jāhiz. hal-hāmūr ṣidtah b-īdi ṣ-ṣubḥ
Come and eat, lunch is ready. I caught this grouper myself this morning.
B
ما شاء الله! تسلم إيدك يا عمي
mā shāʼ allāh! tislam īdak yā ʿammi
Mā shāʼ allāh! Bless your hands, uncle.
A
الله يسلمك، بالعافية عليك يا ولدي
allāh ysallmak, bil-ʿāfya ʿalēk yā wildi
Thank you; enjoy it, son.
B
الله يعافيك. أعترف، ما عليك زود! السمك طازج، والبهارات حلوة
allāh yʿāfīk. aʿtarif, ma ʿalēk zōd! is-simach ṭāzij, w il-bahārāt ḥilwa
God give you health. I have to say, nobody does it better! The fish is fresh, and the spices are lovely.
A
هذا واجبي يا ولدي. كل، لا تستحي
hādha wājbi yā wildi. kil, la tistiḥi
It's my duty, son. Eat, don't be shy.
B
الله لا يهينك يا عمي، بس صدقني شبعت
allāh la yhīnak yā ʿammi, bas ṣaddigni shbaʿt
Thank you so much, uncle, but believe me, I'm full.
A
وين شبعت؟ ما أكلت شي! راشد، حط له
wēn shbaʿt? ma akalt shay! Rāshid, ḥuṭṭ-lah
Full? You've hardly eaten! Rāshid, give him some more.
B
من عيوني، بس والله أكلت وايد. سفرة دايمة يا عمي!
min ʿyūni, bas wallāh akalt wāyid. sufra dāyma yā ʿammi!
Gladly, but honestly I've eaten loads. Thank you for the meal, uncle!
A
دايمة بوجودكم. على كل حال، القهوة! راشد، صب لربعك
dāyma b-wjūdkum. ʿala kill ḥāl, il-gahwa! Rāshid, ṣubb l-rabʿak
As long as you're here to share it. Anyway, coffee! Rāshid, pour for your friends.
B
تامرني على شي ثاني؟ ولّا بنترخص؟
tāmirni ʿala shay thāni? walla binitrakhkhaṣ?
Is there anything else I can do for you? Or may we take our leave?
items: nobody does it better, you can't be beaten (praise) (to a man)
to a woman: ma ʿalēch zōd (ما عليج زود)
thank you so much (lit. may God never humble you) (to a man)
to a woman: allāh la yhīnich (الله لا يهينج)
thank you for the meal (lit. may your table always be full)

title: Same news, office style
goal: At the office, Maryam helps you turn "the report's late, long story" into something you can say in Bū Saʿīd's meeting
tip: In a meeting, keep Gulf grammar but borrow office words: it-taqrīr miḥtāj taʼjīl usbūʿ, il-awlawiyya lit-tansīq, it-tārīkh thābit. Classicisms keep their q: fi l-ḥaqīqa, nitwaqqaʿ. With friends you'd still say it-taqrīr biyitʼakhkhar, giṣṣa ṭawīla!
grammar: register shifting: everyday → office (il-awlawiyya, it-tansīq, thābit; q kept in fi l-ḥaqīqa, nitwaqqaʿ)
dialogue: A
بو سعيد بيسألك في الاجتماع عن التقرير. شو بتقول له؟
Bū Saʿīd biyisʼalak fi l-ijtimāʿ ʿan it-taqrīr. shu bitgūl-lah?
Bū Saʿīd will ask you about the report in the meeting. What will you tell him?
B
بقول: التقرير بيتأخر شوي، قصة طويلة!
bagūl: it-taqrīr biyitʼakhkhar shwayy, giṣṣa ṭawīla!
I'll say: the report's going to be a bit late, long story!
A
هذا كلام شباب! في الاجتماع لازم تكون رسمي أكثر
hādha kalām shabāb! fi l-ijtimāʿ lāzim tkūn rasmi akthar
That's how you'd talk with your mates! In the meeting you need to be more formal.
B
زين. أقصد: في الحقيقة، التقرير محتاج تأجيل أسبوع
zēn. agṣid: fi l-ḥaqīqa, it-taqrīr miḥtāj taʼjīl usbūʿ
OK. I mean: in fact, the report needs to be put back a week. (formal)
A
أحسن وايد. وشو السبب الوحيد؟ لا تقول عشان، قول بسبب
aḥsan wāyid. w shu s-sabab il-waḥīd? la tgūl ʿashān, gūl b-sabab
Much better. And what's the one reason? Don't say ʿashān, say b-sabab.
B
بسبب تأخر البيانات. والأولوية الحين للتنسيق مع القسم الثاني
b-sabab taʼakhkhur il-bayānāt. w il-awlawiyya l-ḥīn lit-tansīq maʿa l-gism ith-thāni
Due to the delay in the data. And the priority now is coordinating with the other department. (formal)
A
ممتاز. والتاريخ اليديد ثابت؟
mumtāz. w it-tārīkh il-yidīd thābit?
Excellent. And is the new date fixed?
B
نتوقع نسلمه يوم الخميس، إن شاء الله
nitwaqqaʿ nsallmah yōm il-khamīs, in shāʼ allāh
We expect to hand it in on Thursday, God willing. (formal)
A
حلو. شفت؟ نفس الشي، بس بأسلوب ثاني. وفي الإيميل اذكر الإجراءات بعد
ḥilu. shift? nafs ish-shay, bas b-uslūb thāni. w fi l-īmēl idhkur il-ijrāʼāt baʿad
Nice. See? The same thing, just in a different style. And in the email, mention the procedures too.
B
الله لا يهينج! يعني في المكتب بسبب، وويا الشباب عشان!
allāh la yhīnich! yaʿni fi l-maktab b-sabab, w wiyya sh-shabāb ʿashān!
Thanks so much! So at the office bi-sabab, and with the lads ʿashān!
items: in coordination with: bit-tansīq maʿa (بالتنسيق مع)
style, way (of doing or saying something)
b-uslūb thāni: in a different style

title: You sound like the news!
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Rāshid there, you answer him in office Arabic; he teases you, and you switch back to plain majlis talk
tip: Office words sound stiff in the majlis: il-mashrūʿ māshi b-khuṭwāt thābta earns you chinnak fi nashrat il-akhbār and la titfalsaf ʿalēna! Switch down to plain words, no kalimāt fakhma: ish-shughul zēn, bas fīh ẓaghiṭ wāyid. In the majlis, talk w inta rāyig.
grammar: register shifting: office → majlis (recycle: chinnak + noun)
dialogue: A
يا هلا بسالم! شو علومك؟ وشو أخبار الشغل؟
yā hala b-Sālim! shu ʿilūmak? w shu akhbār ish-shughul?
Welcome, Sālim! How are things? And how's work?
B
هلا بك يا عمي. الحمد لله، المشروع ماشي بخطوات ثابتة
hala bik yā ʿammi. il-ḥamdu lillāh, il-mashrūʿ māshi b-khuṭwāt thābta
Hello, uncle. Thank God, the project is moving forward steadily.
A
يا سلام! تتكلم كنك في نشرة الأخبار!
yā salām! titkallam chinnak fi nashrat il-akhbār!
My! You talk like you're on the news!
B
السموحة يا عمي، تعودت على تعابير المكتب
is-samūḥa yā ʿammi, tʿawwadt ʿala taʿābīr il-maktab
Sorry, uncle; I've got used to office expressions.
A
ما عليه يا ولدي. هني مجلس، لا تتفلسف علينا! كيف الشغل صج؟
ma ʿalēh yā wildi. hni majlis, la titfalsaf ʿalēna! chēf ish-shughul ṣij?
Never mind, son. This is a majlis; don't get all fancy with us! How's work really?
B
زين، بس الظاهر إن المدير دوم مستعيل، وفيه ضغط وايد
zēn, bas iẓ-ẓāhir inn il-mudīr dōm mistaʿyil, w fīh ẓaghiṭ wāyid
Good, but it looks like the manager's always in a hurry, and there's a lot of pressure.
A
هذا الكلام اللي نفهمه! بلا كلمات فخمة، تكلم وانت رايق
hādha l-kalām illi nifhamah! bala kalimāt fakhma, tkallam w inta rāyig
Now that's talk we understand! No grand words; just talk and relax.
B
صدقت. في الإيميل فصحى، وفي الاجتماع نص إنقليزي
ṣidagt. fi l-īmēl fuṣḥa, w fi l-ijtimāʿ nuṣṣ ingilīzi
True. Fuṣḥā in emails, and half English in meetings.
A
خل الفصحى للإيميل، هذا كلام من الجريدة! وفي المجلس، شو أسلوبك؟
khall il-fuṣḥa lil-īmēl, hādha kalām min il-jarīda! w fi l-majlis, shu uslūbak?
Keep fuṣḥā for emails; that's talk straight out of the newspaper! And in the majlis, what's your style?
B
في المجلس سوالف وبس!
fi l-majlis sawālif w bas!
In the majlis, it's just chatting!
items: the news (bulletin on TV or radio)
don't get all clever, stop using big words (to a man)
to a woman: la titfalsafīn (لا تتفلسفين)
relaxed, at ease (lit. while you're calm) (to a man)
to a woman: w inti rāyga (وانتي رايقة)

title: A toast for Bū Khālid
goal: At the office farewell lunch for Bū Khālid, who is retiring after twenty years, give the team's short formal toast and hand him the team's gift
tip: A toast here is a short formal speech, not a drink. Open with ysharrifni and say who you speak for (b-ism il-farīg), praise him (kint qudwa; tirakt baṣma), close with a wish (nitmanna-lak it-tawfīq), and hand over the gift as ʿarbūn wafāʼ 'a token of loyalty'.
grammar: formal speech (toast): qudwa, baṣma, ajyāl, ʿarbūn wafāʼ
dialogue: A
ها يا سالم؟ يقولون عندك كلمة!
hā yā Sālim? ygūlūn ʿindak kilma!
Well, Sālim? They say you've got a few words for us!
B
يشرفني، باسم الفريق، أقول كلمة بهالمناسبة
ysharrifni, b-ism il-farīg, agūl kilma b-hal-munāsaba
It's an honour, on behalf of the team, to say a few words on this occasion. (formal)
A
تفضل يا ولدي، كلنا آذان صاغية
tfaẓẓal yā wildi, killna ādhān ṣāghya
Go ahead, son; we're all ears.
B
عشرين سنة من التضحيات، وانت تعطي من وقتك وخبرتك للشركة
ʿishrīn sana min it-taẓḥiyāt, w inta tʿaṭi min wagtak w khibratak lish-sharika
Twenty years of sacrifices, giving the company your time and your experience. (formal)
A
الله يخليك، هذا واجبي
allāh ykhallīk, hādha wājbi
Bless you; it was my duty.
B
كنت قدوة لأجيال من الموظفين، وتركت بصمة في كل مشروع بأسلوبك
kint qudwa l-ajyāl min il-muwaẓẓafīn, w tirakt baṣma fi kill mashrūʿ b-uslūbak
You were a role model for generations of staff, and you left your mark on every project in your own way. (formal)
A
كلامك يرفع الراس، ما عليك زود!
kalāmak yirfaʿ ir-rās, ma ʿalēk zōd!
Your words make me proud; nobody does it better!
B
ونتمنى لك التوفيق والصحة بعد التقاعد
w nitmanna-lak it-tawfīq w iṣ-ṣiḥḥa baʿd it-taqāʿud
And we wish you every success and good health in your retirement. (formal)
A
آمين. والله ما توقعت حفلة توديع بهالشكل. ما قصرتوا يا عيالي
āmīn. wallāh ma twaggaʿt ḥaflat tawdīʿ b-hash-shakl. mā gaṣṣartu yā ʿyāli
Amen. Honestly, I didn't expect a farewell party like this. You've all been so kind, my dears.
B
ما سوينا شي. هذي الهدية عربون وفاء وامتنان
mā sawwēna shay. hādhi l-hadiyya ʿarbūn wafāʼ w imtinān
It's nothing. This gift is a token of loyalty and gratitude. (formal)
items: a role model, an example (to follow) (formal)
you left your mark (to a man); I left my mark
to a woman: tirakti baṣma (تركتي بصمة)
a token of loyalty, a token of thanks (formal)
task: This week: record a 2-minute toast (formal) for a friend's graduation or a colleague who's leaving. Open with ysharrifni and b-ism…, praise one quality (kint qudwa, tirakt baṣma), and close with nitmanna-lak it-tawfīq. Then record 30 seconds saying the same thing to the friend over karak, the way friends talk: no fuṣḥā words, and as much ḥilu and wāyid as you like.

title: Welcome to our company
goal: At the office, a teacher brings a school group to visit; on Bū Saʿīd's behalf, give a short formal welcome, then switch back to everyday talk for the tour
tip: A formal welcome: ahlan wa sahlan bikum (the wa is fuṣḥā, kept in this phrase), who you speak for (bin-niyāba ʿan mudīrna), and what comes first (nubdha ʿan sharikatna 'a short overview of our company'). Then drop back to everyday Gulf: jōla fi l-mabna, tāmrūn ʿala shay thāni?, yalla yā shabāb.
grammar: formal welcome: ahlan wa sahlan bikum, bin-niyāba ʿan, nubdha ʿan
dialogue: A
السلام عليكم. نحن وفد المدرسة، عندنا موعد زيارة اليوم
as-salāmu ʿalaykum. niḥin wafd il-madrasa, ʿindana mawʿid zyāra l-yōm
Peace be upon you. We're the school group; we've got a visit booked for today.
B
وعليكم السلام، حياكم الله! تفضلوا
wa ʿalaykum is-salām, ḥayyākum allāh! tfaẓẓalu
And peace be upon you. Welcome! Come in.
A
الله يحييكم. الطلاب كلهم هني، وضروري نخلص قبل الظهر
allāh yḥayyīkum. iṭ-ṭullāb killhum hni, w ẓarūri nkhalliṣ gabil iẓ-ẓuhur
Thank you. The students are all here, and we really need to finish before noon.
B
أهلا وسهلا بكم. بالنيابة عن مديرنا بو سعيد، يسعدنا نرحب فيكم
ahlan wa sahlan bikum. bin-niyāba ʿan mudīrna Bū Saʿīd, yisʿidna nraḥḥib fīkum
Welcome. On behalf of our manager, Bū Saʿīd, we're delighted to welcome you. (formal)
A
الله يحفظك. الشباب متحمسين وايد
allāh yiḥfaẓak. ish-shabāb mitḥammsīn wāyid
God keep you. The boys are really excited.
B
في البداية، نبذة قصيرة عن شركتنا وشعارها
fi l-bidāya, nubdha gaṣīra ʿan sharikatna w shiʿārha
First, a short overview of our company and its logo. (formal)
A
ممتاز. وبعدها؟
mumtāz. w baʿd-ha?
Excellent. And after that?
B
جولة في المبنى، والأسئلة في الآخر
jōla fi l-mabna, w il-asʼila fi l-ākhir
A tour of the building, and questions at the end.
A
إن شاء الله. مشكورين على الاستقبال، ما عليكم زود
in shāʼ allāh. mashkūrīn ʿala l-istiqbāl, ma ʿalēkum zōd
God willing. Thank you for having us; nobody does it better.
B
العفو. تامرون على شي ثاني؟ يلا يا شباب، من هني!
il-ʿafu. tāmrūn ʿala shay thāni? yalla yā shabāb, min hni!
You're welcome. Anything else you need? Come on, lads, this way!
items: the wa ('and') is fuṣḥā, kept in this set phrase
a short overview, a brief introduction (formal)

title: Three languages, one meeting
goal: At the office, plan tomorrow's client presentation with Maryam: which parts go in fuṣḥā, which in English, and which in Emirati
tip: Choosing a language is part of the job: the official letter bil-fuṣḥa, with il-khitim on it; the slides kill fagra b-lughtēn; the talk in Emirati. Office talk is a khalīṭ, because some terms ma lha tarjama wāẓḥa. Ask b-ay lugha? 'in which language?'
grammar: triglossia: il-fuṣḥa for writing, English for terms, Emirati for talk
dialogue: A
العرض باكر للعميل. نسوي الشرايح بالإنقليزي ولّا بالعربي؟
il-ʿarẓ bāchir lil-ʿamīl. nsawwi sh-sharāyiḥ bil-ingilīzi walla bil-ʿarabi?
The presentation for the client is tomorrow. Do we do the slides in English or Arabic?
B
العميل منو؟
il-ʿamīl minu?
Who's the client?
A
جهة حكومية، عشان جي الخطاب الرسمي لازم بالفصحى، وعليه الختم والشعار
jiha ḥukūmiyya, ʿashān chī l-khiṭāb ir-rasmi lāzim bil-fuṣḥa, w ʿalēh il-khitim w ish-shiʿār
A government body, so the official letter has to be in fuṣḥā, with the stamp and the logo on it.
B
والشرايح؟ والكلام في الاجتماع؟
w ish-sharāyiḥ? w il-kalām fi l-ijtimāʿ?
And the slides? And the talking in the meeting?
A
الشرايح كل فقرة بلغتين، بس الكلام باللهجة. هذا أسلوبنا
ish-sharāyiḥ kill fagra b-lughtēn, bas il-kalām bil-lahja. hādha uslūbna
On the slides, every paragraph in two languages, but the talking in dialect. That's how we do it.
B
يعني ثلاث لغات في اجتماع واحد! ضروري؟
yaʿni thalāth lughāt fi jtimāʿ wāḥid! ẓarūri?
So three languages in one meeting! Is that really necessary?
A
هيه، كلامنا خليط. المصطلحات التقنية نقولها بالإنقليزي
hē, kalāmna khalīṭ. il-muṣṭalaḥāt it-tiqniyya ngūlha bil-ingilīzi
Yes, the way we talk is a mix. The technical terms we say in English.
B
منطقي، لأن بعضها ما لها ترجمة واضحة
manṭiqi, lann baʿaẓha ma lha tarjama wāẓḥa
That makes sense, because some of them have no clear translation.
A
بالضبط. وانت بتقدم الأرقام، بأي لغة؟
biẓ-ẓabṭ. w inta bitgaddim il-argām, b-ay lugha?
Exactly. And you're presenting the figures: in which language?
B
بالعربي، عشان أتدرب. وإذا علقت، الإنقليزي موجود!
bil-ʿarabi, ʿashān atdarrab. w idha ʿligt, il-ingilīzi mawjūd!
In Arabic, for the practice. And if I get stuck, there's always English!
items: fuṣḥā, Modern Standard Arabic (for writing, news and school)
it has no translation, there's no word for it (a feminine or plural thing)
a masculine thing: ma lah tarjama (ما له ترجمة)
one language: lugha (لغة); two languages: lughtēn (لغتين)
a paragraph, a section (of a text)
culture: Emiratis live with three languages. Emirati Arabic is for everyday talk; fuṣḥā is for education, public speeches, literature, Islamic studies and TV news; and English is the common language with people who don't speak Arabic. A young Emirati may chat in Emirati with a friend, read a newspaper in fuṣḥā and switch to English in class, all in one day.

title: On air: why Emirati?
goal: On the university radio, the presenter interviews you about learning Emirati Arabic; answer his formal questions in educated Gulf Arabic
tip: On air, structure your answers with educated Gulf linkers: bin-nisba li 'for me', min ṣōb … w min ṣōb thāni 'on the one hand … on the other', b-shakl ʿāmm 'on the whole'. The presenter's lines are formal (ḥaddithna ʿan tajrubtak); your grammar can stay Gulf.
grammar: educated spoken Arabic in an interview: bin-nisba li, min ṣōb … w min ṣōb thāni, b-shakl ʿāmm
dialogue: A
مستمعينا الكرام، أهلا بكم من جديد في إذاعة الجامعة. ضيفنا اليوم في الأستوديو طالب بريطاني
mustamiʿīna l-kirām, ahlan bikum min jadīd fi idhāʿat il-jāmʿa. ẓēfna l-yōm fi l-istūdyo ṭālib brīṭāni
Dear listeners, welcome back to university radio. Our guest in the studio today is a British student. (formal)
B
أهلا وسهلا، يشرفني أكون معكم
ahlan wa sahlan, ysharrifni akūn maʿākum
Hello, it's an honour to be with you. (formal)
A
حدثنا عن تجربتك: ليش اخترت اللهجة مب الفصحى؟
ḥaddithna ʿan tajrubtak: lēsh ikhtart il-lahja mub il-fuṣḥa?
Tell us about your experience: why did you choose the dialect and not fuṣḥā? (formal)
B
بالنسبة لي، عندي شغف باللهجة، والناس هني يتكلمونها
bin-nisba li, ʿindi shaghaf bil-lahja, w in-nās hni yitkallamūnha
For me, I have a passion for the dialect, and people here speak it. (formal)
A
جميل. وشو أكبر تحدي واجهته؟
jamīl. w shu akbar taḥaddi wājahtah?
Lovely. And what's the biggest challenge you've faced? (formal)
B
من صوب، حروف مثل العين والحا. ومن صوب ثاني، الناس يتكلمون بسرعة
min ṣōb, ḥurūf mithil il-ʿēn w il-ḥā. w min ṣōb thāni, in-nās yitkallamūn b-surʿa
On the one hand, letters like ʿayn and ḥā. And on the other hand, people talk fast. (formal)
A
وشو رأيك بالعربي بين الأجيال اليوم؟
w shu raʼyak bil-ʿarabi bēn il-ajyāl il-yōm?
And what do you think of Arabic across the generations today?
B
بشكل عام، كلام الشباب خليط، بس العربي باقي قوي
b-shakl ʿāmm, kalām ish-shabāb khalīṭ, bas il-ʿarabi bāgi gawi
On the whole, young people's talk is a mix, but Arabic is still strong. (formal)
A
نشكرك على هالحوار. مستمعينا، بعد الفاصل نرجع لكم
nishkurak ʿala hal-ḥiwār. mustamiʿīna, baʿd il-fāṣil nirjaʿ lakum
Thank you for this conversation. Listeners, we'll be back after the break. (formal)
B
الشكر لكم، والشرف لي
ish-shukr lakum, w ish-sharaf li
Thank you, and the honour's mine.
items: tell us about your experience (formal) (to a man)
(recognise); to a woman: ḥaddithīna ʿan tajrubtich
ʿindi shaghaf b-: I have a passion for
a conversation, an interview, a dialogue (formal)
we'll be back after the break (formal)
culture: Fuṣḥā is the language of UAE TV news, education and public speeches, but how much of it a speaker uses depends on the occasion and on the speaker's sense of register. It is quite normal to hear Emirati Arabic in a public speech, mixed with some high-register words and fixed phrases taken from fuṣḥā.

title: Off air
goal: Straight after the interview, the presenter drops the formal voice; talk about your nerves, the mixing, and when the interview goes out
tip: The same speaker shifts register in seconds: off air it's khalāṣ, khilaṣ il-lāyf, ṭilaʿna min il-hawa. irtāḥ! Then ask about the repeat: mita l-iʿāda? ʿala ay mōja?
grammar: register shifting: formal → everyday as soon as the mic is off
dialogue: A
خلاص، خلص اللايف، طلعنا من الهوا. ارتاح يا سالم!
khalāṣ, khilaṣ il-lāyf, ṭilaʿna min il-hawa. irtāḥ yā Sālim!
That's it, the live show's over, we're off air. Relax, Sālim!
B
الحمد لله! والله توترت وايد على الهوا
il-ḥamdu lillāh! wallāh twattart wāyid ʿala l-hawa
Thank God! Honestly, I got really nervous on air.
A
ما بان عليك أبد، وكان حوار حلو. صوتك واضح في المايك
ma bān ʿalēk abad, w kān ḥiwār ḥilu. ṣōtak wāẓiḥ fi l-māyk
It didn't show at all, and it was a good conversation. Your voice is clear on the mic.
B
بشكل عام زين، بس حسيت كلامي خليط فصحى ولهجة
b-shakl ʿāmm zēn, bas ḥassēt kalāmi khalīṭ fuṣḥa w lahja
On the whole fine, but I felt my talk was a mix of fuṣḥā and dialect.
A
عادي، كلنا جي. حتى أنا أبدا بالفصحى وأكمل باللهجة
ʿādi, killna chī. ḥatta ana abda bil-fuṣḥa w akammil bil-lahja
That's normal; we're all like that. Even I start in fuṣḥā and carry on in dialect.
B
ومتى الإعادة؟ وعلى أي موجة؟
w mita l-iʿāda? w ʿala ay mōja?
And when's the repeat? And on which frequency?
A
الإعادة الخميس الياي، الساعة ثمان الصبح، على نفس الموجة
il-iʿāda l-khamīs il-yāy, is-sāʿa thamān iṣ-ṣubḥ, ʿala nafs il-mōja
The repeat's next Thursday, at eight in the morning, on the same frequency.
B
زين، بقول لفهد وبو راشد يسمعونها
zēn, bagūl l-Fahad w Bū Rāshid yismaʿūnha
Great, I'll tell Fahad and Bū Rāshid to listen to it.
A
وصورنا لقطة بالكاميرا بعد، بنحطها أونلاين
w ṣawwarna lagṭa bil-kāmīra baʿad, binḥuṭṭha ōnlāyn
And we filmed a short clip on camera too; we'll put it online.
B
أكيد! بس المرة الياية بتكلم باللهجة من البداية في البرنامج
akīd! bas il-marra l-yāya batkallam bil-lahja min il-bidāya fi l-barnāmij
Great! But next time on the programme I'll talk in dialect from the start.
items: on which frequency?: ʿala ay mōja? (على أي موجة؟)
the programme, the show (on radio or TV)
on the mic, into the microphone
the live show, the live broadcast

title: Fahad hears about the radio
goal: On a video call, Fahad has heard you were on the radio; tell him how it went, and compare how your languages are slipping, his at work and yours in the majlis
tip: Say a language is slipping with tbahdalat 'it's gone to pieces': ʿarabiyyti tbahdalat, ingilīziyyti tbahdalat. Name the mix with mazīj, and the fix with atmarran 'I practise': lāzim atmarran, nitmarran kill usbūʿ. Fahad's Kuwaiti forms (shinu, shdaʿwa, ēh) are for recognition.
grammar: saying a language is slipping: ʿarabiyyti tbahdalat, kalāmi mazīj; fixing it: lāzim atmarran
dialogue: A
هلا والله! سمعت إنك طلعت بالراديو، وشفت اللقطة! شلون كانت؟
hala wallāh! simaʿt innak ṭilaʿt bir-rādyo, w shift il-lagṭa! shlōn kānat?
Hey! I heard you were on the radio, and I saw the clip! How did it go?
B
هلا فيك! كان حوار حلو، بس توترت
hala fīk! kān ḥiwār ḥilu, bas twattart
Hi! It was a good conversation, but I got nervous.
A
شدعوه! انت تتكلم أحسن مني. أنا في الدوام كله إنقليزي
shdaʿwa! inta titkallam aḥsan minni. ana fi d-dawām killah ingilīzi
Come off it! You speak better than me. At work, everything's English for me.
B
صج؟ حتى الاجتماعات؟
ṣij? ḥatta l-ijtimāʿāt?
Really? Even the meetings?
A
إيه، وعربيتي تبهدلت، حتى اللكنة تغيرت. كلامي مزيج
ēh, w ʿarabiyyti tbahdalat, ḥatta l-lakna tghayyarat. kalāmi mazīj
Yes, and my Arabic's gone to pieces; even my accent has changed. The way I talk is a mix.
B
وأنا بالعكس: إنقليزيتي تبهدلت!
w ana bil-ʿaks: ingilīziyyti tbahdalat!
And it's the other way round for me: my English has gone to pieces!
A
حلوة هذي! بس شنو سألوك بالمقابلة؟
ḥilwa hādhi! bas shinu saʼlūk bil-mugābla?
That's a good one! But what did they ask you in the interview?
B
باختصار: ليش اللهجة، وعن شغفي فيها، وشلون يتكلم الشباب
b-ikhtiṣār: lēsh il-lahja, w ʿan shaghafi fīha, w shlōn yitkallam ish-shabāb
In short: why the dialect, my passion for it, and how young people talk.
A
لازم أتمرن وياك. تسوي وياي نفس المقابلة، بس بالكويتي؟
lāzim atmarran wiyyāk. tsawwi wiyyāy nafs il-mugābla, bas bil-kwēti?
I need to practise with you. Will you do the same interview with me, but in Kuwaiti?
B
اتفقنا! نتمرن كل أسبوع: انت تسأل، وأنا أرد بالإماراتي
ittafagna! nitmarran kill usbūʿ: inta tisʼal, w ana arudd bil-imārāti
Deal! We'll practise every week: you ask, and I'll answer in Emirati.
items: you were on the radio (to a man); I was on the radio
to a woman: ṭilaʿti bir-rādyo (طلعتي بالراديو); (recognise)
it (f.) has gone to pieces, it's got into a mess (friends only)
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner, do a 10-minute mock radio interview about your Arabic. They ask in a formal style; you answer in educated Gulf Arabic (bin-nisba li, min ṣōb…, b-shakl ʿāmm). Then switch: off air, retell the interview for 2 minutes the way you'd tell Sēf on a video call, mixing in as much English as he would.

title: Checkpoint 5.3: the radio star in the majlis
goal: Checkpoint: in Bū Rāshid's majlis, he heard your radio interview; take his teasing, explain your registers, and take your leave properly
tip: Review: thank an elder with allāh la yhīnak; keep sōri and yēs for the pitch (yā salām in the majlis); quote your on-air style (bin-nisba li …); welcome a group with ahlan wa sahlan bikum, bin-niyāba ʿan …; leave with binitrakhkhaṣ?, and offer help with tāmirni ʿala shay thāni?
grammar: checkpoint 5.3 (s5u032–s5u045): honorifics, borrowed interjections, register shifting
dialogue: A
يا هلا بالنجم! سويت ضجة! سمعنا البث في السيارة، الله يحفظك من الحسد
yā hala bin-najim! sawwēt ẓajja! simaʿna l-bathth fi s-sayyāra, allāh yiḥfaẓak min il-ḥasad
Welcome, star! You've caused a stir! We heard the broadcast in the car; God protect you from envy.
B
الله لا يهينك، بس توترت على الهوا
allāh la yhīnak, bas twattart ʿala l-hawa
That's kind of you, but I got nervous on air.
A
ما بان عليك. بس ليش تكلمت كنك في نشرة الأخبار؟
ma bān ʿalēk. bas lēsh tkallamt chinnak fi nashrat il-akhbār?
It didn't show. But why did you talk like you were on the news?
B
هذا أسلوب الراديو: «بالنسبة لي، عندي شغف باللهجة». وفي المجلس سوالف وبس
hādha uslūb ir-rādyo: "bin-nisba li, ʿindi shaghaf bil-lahja". w fi l-majlis sawālif w bas
That's the radio style: "For me, I have a passion for the dialect." (formal) And in the majlis it's just chatting.
A
زين تسوي. وراشد يقول إنك تقول «واو» في الملعب!
zēn tsawwi. w Rāshid ygūl innak tgūl "wāw" fi l-malʿab!
Good for you. And Rāshid says you say "wow" on the pitch!
B
سوري ويس ويا الشباب بس. قدامك يا سلام!
sōri w yēs wiyya sh-shabāb bas. jiddāmak yā salām!
"Sorry" and "yes!" only with the lads. In front of you, yā salām!
A
تكلمت زين! طرش لي الرابط، أبي أشوفك في القناة. وإذا زارك وفد، شو تقول؟
tkallamt zēn! ṭarrish-li r-rābiṭ, abi ashūfak fi l-qanāh. w idha zārak wafd, shu tgūl?
You spoke well! Send me the link; I want to see you on the channel. And if a delegation visits you, what do you say?
B
من عيوني. أقول: أهلا وسهلا بكم، بالنيابة عن الفريق! وإذا ما شي لازم، بنترخص؟
min ʿyūni. agūl: ahlan wa sahlan bikum, bin-niyāba ʿan il-farīg! w idha ma shay lāzim, binitrakhkhaṣ?
Gladly. I say: "Welcome, on behalf of the team!" (formal) And if there's nothing you need, may we take our leave?
A
وين؟ بدري! بس يلا، الله يوفقكم
wēn? badri! bas yalla, allāh ywaffigkum
What, already? It's early! But off you go; God grant you success.
B
آمين يا عمي. تامرني على شي ثاني؟
āmīn yā ʿammi. tāmirni ʿala shay thāni?
Amen, uncle. Anything else I can do for you?
items: God protect you from envy (after praising someone) (to a man)
(recognise); to a woman: allāh yiḥfaẓich min il-ḥasad
the link (to a website or a clip)
a stir, a fuss, a buzz (sawwēt ẓajja: you've caused a stir)
